evidence_quote: BEIC reports 39,821 digital resources, 98,327 bibliographic records, and 5,617 authors.
limitation: The total is multidisciplinary and includes non-text, non-Italian, and in-copyright material.

evidence_quote: BEIC states that its digital-library images are freely accessible, downloadable, and reusable; public-domain reproductions remain public domain, copyrighted BEIC-held works are CC BY-SA, and catalog/OAI-PMH metadata is CC0.
supports_decision: Establishes reusable digital objects and open metadata subject to exact work status.
limitation: The image license does not establish corrected OCR or identify Italian literary text automatically.

evidence_quote: Incunaboli in volgare contains more than 1,600 incunabula from about 70 libraries and more than 200,000 freely consultable images with technical and management metadata.
supports_decision: Pins the archive-scale image inventory and confirms metadata availability.
limitation: No corrected transcription, OCR download, or corpus-text reuse grant is advertised.

evidence_quote: Scrittori d’Italia comprises 287 volumes, 179 works, and 125,171 image-text pages; the images are freely available under Laterza's permission.
supports_decision: Pins the complete advertised scope and confirms an image rather than transcription layer.
limitation: Image availability does not establish an OCR/full-text layer or avoid overlap with BibIt.

evidence_quote: DiaCORIS exposes 1861-2001 sections and grants query access exclusively for scientific research with no economic benefit.
supports_decision: Confirms the historical slice and non-commercial research query route.
limitation: It does not grant bulk text, redistribution, derivative-dataset, or model-training permission.

evidence_quote: The ELTeC Italian release contains 36 level-1 novels; all included texts are public domain and the textual markup is CC BY 4.0.
supports_decision: Establishes release size, text status, markup license, contributors, and source families.
limitation: The release overlaps BibIt/CLiGS sources and includes early-twentieth-century material, so it requires capped, record-level inventory.

evidence_quote: Gallica's SRU API searches the digital collection and exposes OCR-quality values from 0 to 100.
supports_decision: Supports a metadata-only inventory and a later measured OCR-quality gate.
limitation: API access does not itself permit reuse of digitized documents.

evidence_quote: BnF API terms permit dataset downloads but require separate Gallica content terms or prior authorization for digitized-document reuse; BnF metadata is Etalab Open Licence 2.0 with source and update-date credit.
supports_decision: Permits bounded metadata discovery with attribution.
limitation: Corpus-text training remains blocked until the exact Gallica content and item rights pass.

evidence_quote: The Books API is a search and access interface; availability varies with copyright, contract, legal restrictions, and user location.
supports_decision: Supports discovery of editions that can be located in reusable archives.
limitation: API discovery and preview availability are not reusable corpus-text provenance.

evidence_quote: Google Books API use is governed by the Books API and Google APIs terms, with removal duties for supplied content.
supports_decision: Supports metadata discovery under the API terms.
limitation: The terms do not grant a blanket corpus-text training or bulk-download right.

evidence_quote: The official HathiTrust terms page returned an automated-access challenge to this audit client.
supports_decision: Records that first-party permission evidence could not be pinned.
limitation: No training, bulk-download, or redistribution permission may be inferred from full-view status.

evidence_quote: Internet Archive documents automated access for bots, AI agents, and LLMs and requires descriptive user agents, delays, and rate-limit handling.
supports_decision: Authorizes a rate-limited metadata inventory through documented services.
limitation: Operational access guidance is not a blanket license for item text.

supports_decision: Measures the broad metadata candidate ceiling for Italian texts dated no later than 1900.
limitation: Language/date metadata is noisy; the count is not a rights-cleared or OCR-quality-passing corpus.

evidence_quote: The official collection directory reports 291 digital collections and distinguishes full-text and digital-text discovery routes.
supports_decision: Measures the collection-level discovery universe before item inventory.
limitation: Collection count is not a count of reusable Italian primary-text documents.

evidence_quote: Internet Culturale permits non-commercial sharing and transformation of hosted digital content with attribution and ShareAlike, subject to different item-specific indications; metadata is CC0 1.0.
supports_decision: Establishes a compatible non-commercial reuse route and its attribution/share-alike duties.
limitation: Partner sites and item-specific notices can override portal defaults; web-resolution files are not automatically primary text.

evidence_quote: MIDIA documents downloadable CSV query results and links from concordance rows to the source text and work metadata.
supports_decision: Supports a bounded source-list and access inventory.
limitation: A query-result interface is not yet a verified bulk release endpoint.

evidence_quote: MIDIA reports about 7.8 million occurrences from about 800 texts spanning the thirteenth to mid-twentieth century and distributes the corpus under CC BY-NC 4.0.
supports_decision: Establishes non-commercial reuse terms, composition scale, and attribution duty.
limitation: The corpus crosses 1900 and still requires period filtering, source-level deduplication, and an access-method audit.

evidence_quote: The official TLIO landing page exposes an interrogation menu.
limitation: No bulk text, license, redistribution, or model-training permission is stated.
